data.howToName: How to boil eggs for deviled eggs

description: Deviled eggs need fully set yolks: a large fridge egg takes 10 minutes 10 seconds to hard-boil. Times by size, plus peeling and mashing notes.

faqs.answer: A large fridge egg takes 10 minutes 10 seconds to hard-boil. A medium egg takes 9 minutes 15 seconds, an extra-large 10 minutes 55 seconds, and a jumbo 11 minutes 45 seconds. The yolk must be fully set to mash smooth.
faqs.question: How long do I boil eggs for deviled eggs?

faqs.answer: They were overcooked or cooled slowly. The grey-green layer is iron sulfide, formed when the yolk stays hot too long. Stop on time and move the eggs straight to ice water for 10 minutes.
faqs.question: Why are my deviled egg yolks grey?

faqs.answer: Boil the eggs up to a week ahead: hard-cooked eggs keep up to 7 days refrigerated in the shell, per USDA guidance. Once filled, deviled eggs are best within 4 days, and they should not sit out for more than 2 hours.
faqs.question: How far ahead can I make deviled eggs?

faqs.answer: Yes, 9 minutes 15 seconds from the fridge. The halves will be smaller, so you will want more eggs for the same crowd. Keep all the eggs one size so they finish together.
faqs.question: Can I use medium eggs for deviled eggs?

faqs.answer: The eggs were too fresh. An egg a week or so old has a bigger air cell and the membrane pulls away cleanly; a very fresh egg sticks and tears the white. Buy the eggs a week ahead, and give them a 10 minute ice bath before peeling.
faqs.question: Why do my whites tear when I peel them?

felicityNote: Deviled eggs disappear first at every gathering I have ever been to. Boil a dozen even if you think you need six.

parts.meaning: The constant from the egg's thermal properties: density 1.038 g per cubic cm, specific heat 3.7, thermal conductivity 0.0054.
The weight of the egg in grams. A large egg is 57 g (USDA size).
The starting temperature of the egg: 4°C from the fridge, 20°C at room temperature.
The boiling point of the water: 100°C at sea level, lower at altitude.
The target temperature at the edge of the yolk: 84°C for hard-boiled.
The yolk edge factor. The yolk is about a third of the egg, so its edge sits about 69 percent of the way from the center to the shell.

formula.text: Time = 27 × M^(2/3) × ln(0.76 × (Tegg - Twater) / (Tyolk - Twater)). For a large fridge egg at sea level, hard-boiled for deviled eggs: 27 × 57^(2/3) × ln(0.76 × (4 - 100) / (84 - 100)) = 608 seconds, about 10 minutes 10 seconds.

howToSteps.name: Buy the eggs a week ahead
howToSteps.text: Older eggs peel cleanly, because the air cell has grown. Very fresh eggs stick and tear the whites.

howToSteps.name: Boil the water first
howToSteps.text: Bring a saucepan of water to a full rolling boil. The formula assumes the egg goes into water that is already boiling.

howToSteps.name: Lower the eggs in and time it
howToSteps.text: Lower each egg in gently on a spoon. Boil a large fridge egg for 10 minutes 10 seconds, a medium for 9 minutes 15 seconds, an extra-large for 10 minutes 55 seconds, and a jumbo for 11 minutes 45 seconds.

howToSteps.name: Ice bath
howToSteps.text: Move the eggs straight to ice water for 10 minutes. This stops the cooking, keeps the yolks pale yellow, and shrinks the egg slightly inside the shell so it peels smooth.

howToSteps.name: Peel, halve, and mash
howToSteps.text: Peel under cold running water, halve lengthwise, and push the yolks through a fine sieve or mash them well before mixing the filling.

lede: Deviled eggs need hard-boiled eggs with fully set, mashable yolks: a large fridge egg takes 10 minutes 10 seconds. A wet center will not mash smooth, and an overcooked yolk turns chalky and grey.

title: How Long to Boil Eggs for Deviled Eggs
tutorial: A deviled egg starts with a hard-boiled egg, and the yolk has to be fully set to mash smooth. A large fridge egg takes 10 minutes 10 seconds. Any less and the center stays wet and the filling turns lumpy; any more and the yolk dries out and the grey-green ring appears. The window is about two minutes wide, which is generous for eggs but not infinite.

Older eggs are the secret to deviled eggs, because they peel cleanly. An egg that is a week or so old has a bigger air cell, and the membrane pulls away from the white instead of tearing it. Very fresh eggs stick and pock the whites, which matters when the white is the serving dish. Buy the eggs a week ahead if you can.

Size sets the time: a medium egg needs 9 minutes 15 seconds, an extra-large 10 minutes 55 seconds, and a jumbo 11 minutes 45 seconds. If you are boiling a dozen for a party, keep them all one size so they all finish together. Mixed sizes mean some yolks mash smooth and some stay wet.

The ice bath matters twice over for deviled eggs. Ten minutes in ice water stops the cooking, so the yolks stay pale yellow instead of greying, and it shrinks the egg slightly inside the shell, so the whites peel smooth. Peel under cold running water, starting at the wide end where the air pocket sits.

Halve the eggs lengthwise and push the yolks through a fine sieve or mash them well before you mix in the filling. A sieve gives the smoothest filling with the least effort, and it is worth the extra minute when the eggs are the center of the table.
